group.passage:
Pick up a sheet of printer paper almost anywhere outside North America, and it will probably measure 210 by 297 millimeters. The numbers look random, but they hide a neat piece of geometry. The long side of an A4 sheet is about 1.414 times its short side, a ratio known as the square root of two. A sheet of this shape has a useful property: if you cut it in half with a line parallel to its short edges, each half has exactly the same shape as the sheet you started with.
The whole system grows from one large sheet called A0. Since the ratio makes it impossible for both sides to be round numbers, the designers fixed the area instead, so A0 covers one square meter and measures 841 by 1,189 millimeters. Every other size is made by halving the one before it, which makes A4 one sixteenth of a square meter. Whenever halving produced half a millimeter, the result was rounded down, so two small sheets never take up more room than the larger one they came from. Weights become easy to work out, too: ordinary office paper weighs 80 grams per square meter, so a single A4 sheet weighs 5 grams.
The idea itself is older than the standard. In 1786 the German scientist Georg Christoph Lichtenberg praised the ratio in a letter and remarked that paper of this shape was already easy to find. In 1798 a French law on taxing paper listed several formats that match today’s sizes exactly, but they soon dropped out of use. More than a century later, Walter Porstmann worked out the same system in Germany without knowing of the French one, and in 1922 it became the national standard DIN 476, replacing a confusing mix of older sizes.
Other countries followed, from Belgium in 1924 to Australia in 1974, and in 1975 the series became the international standard ISO 216. The United States and Canada are the main exceptions. Their Letter paper measures 216 by 279 millimeters, and the sizes in their family switch between two different shapes, so shrinking two pages onto one sheet always leaves part of the paper blank. With A sizes, a copier set to 71 percent fits two A4 pages neatly onto a single A4 sheet.

translation_zh.text:
在北美以外的幾乎任何地方拿起一張印表機用紙，它大概都是 210 × 297 公釐。這些數字看似隨意，卻藏著一個巧妙的幾何原理。A4 紙的長邊大約是短邊的 1.414 倍，這個比例就是二的平方根。這種形狀的紙有個實用的特性：如果沿著與短邊平行的線把它裁成兩半，每一半的形狀都和原本那張完全一樣。
整個系統是從一張叫做 A0 的大紙開始的。由於這個比例讓長、短邊不可能都是整數，設計者改為固定面積：A0 的面積是一平方公尺，尺寸是 841 × 1,189 公釐。其他每個尺寸都是把前一個尺寸對半得來，所以 A4 是十六分之一平方公尺。每當對半後出現半公釐，就把結果無條件捨去，這樣兩張小紙加起來絕不會比裁出它們的那張大紙還大。重量也變得容易計算：一般辦公用紙每平方公尺重 80 公克，所以一張 A4 重 5 公克。
這個構想本身比標準還早出現。1786 年，德國科學家利希滕貝格在一封信中稱讚這個比例，並提到這種形狀的紙當時已經很容易買到。1798 年，法國一項紙張課稅的法律列出了幾種與今天尺寸完全相同的格式，但它們很快就不再使用。一百多年後，波斯特曼在不知道法國制度的情況下，在德國重新想出了同一套系統；1922 年，它成為德國國家標準 DIN 476，取代了先前雜亂的各種舊尺寸。
其他國家陸續跟進，從 1924 年的比利時到 1974 年的澳洲；1975 年，這個系列成為國際標準 ISO 216。美國和加拿大是主要的例外。他們的 Letter 紙是 216 × 279 公釐，而同一系列的尺寸在兩種不同的形狀之間交替，所以把兩頁縮印到一張紙上，總會留下一部分空白。如果用 A 系列，只要把影印機設定為 71%，就能把兩頁 A4 剛好印在一張 A4 上。
【表】ISO A 系列 A0 到 A6 的短邊、長邊（公釐）與約略面積（平方公尺）：A0 841、1189、1；A1 594、841、1/2；A2 420、594、1/4；A3 297、420、1/8；A4 210、297、1/16；A5 148、210、1/32；A6 105、148、1/64。

open_tasks.prompt: In 1–2 English sentences, explain why the A series uses the square root of two as the ratio between the long and short sides of a sheet.
reference_answers: The square root of two lets a sheet be cut in half and still keep the same shape, so every size in the series can be made from the one before it.
Because a sheet with this ratio keeps its shape when halved, pages can be shrunk or enlarged from one size to another without leaving blank space.
